english.title: Keeper of food producing animal fail to record details of veterinary medicinal product at time purchased or acquired
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being the keeper of a food-producing animal, namely **(..SPECIFY ANIMAL..) for which a veterinary medicinal product, namely **(..SPECIFY PRODUCT..) was

(A)_[bought,]_
(B)_[acquired,]_

failed at the time to record

(C)_[the name of the product and the batch number]_
(D)_[the date of acquisition]_
(E)_[the quantity acquired]_
(F)_[the name and address of the supplier]_
(G)_[**(..WHERE MORE THAN ONE OF THE ABOVE APPLIES - SPECIFY..)]_
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 19(1), 43(k) and 44(1) of the Veterinary Medicines Regulations 2013.
english.pointstoprove:
date and Location
keeper of a food producing animal
fail to record at the time of purchase of veterinary medicinal product
name of product/batch number/date of acquisition/quantity acquired/name and address of supplier

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

Note
Note that for offences committed since 12 March 2015, section 85 of the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment of Offenders Act 2012 removes the limits on certain fines given by the Magistrates' Courts. Offences that were previously punishable by fines of 'prescribed sums' and that were limited to 'not exceeding level 5 on the standard scale' or 'not exceeding the statutory maximum', are now punishable by a fine of any amount.
